scope: Deuteronomy 19–26, all 179 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public Deuteronomy 22:30 binds Hebrew 23:1; public 23:1–25 binds Hebrew 23:2–26. All other verses in chapters 19–26 align directly. All 179 original XML records, including written/read and numbering notes, are hashed in full.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine removal, Israel's dispossession, and occupation of existing homes as the setting for refuge laws.
verses.before: “When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and live in their cities and houses,
verses.after: “When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land he is giving you, and you dispossess them and settle in their towns and houses,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When the LORD your God cuts off the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and live in their cities and houses,

verses.rationale: Retains three designated towns and the land-gift formula, completing the preceding condition.
verses.before: you will set apart three cities for yourself among your land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
verses.after: set apart three towns within the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the midst of your land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.

verses.rationale: Makes the travel provision and threefold distribution clear; killer remains broader than intentional murderer.
verses.before: You will prepare the road for yourself and divide into three parts the territory of your land that the LORD your God causes you to inherit, so that every manslayer may flee there.
verses.after: Prepare the roads and divide into three regions the land the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, so that anyone who kills someone can flee there.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall prepare the road for yourself and divide into three parts the territory of your land that the LORD your God causes you to inherit, so that every manslayer may flee there.

verses.rationale: Preserves both lack of intention and lack of prior hatred as the qualifying conditions.
verses.before: “And this is the case of the manslayer who may flee there and live: whoever strikes his neighbor without intent and did not hate him previously—
verses.after: This is the case of someone who may flee there and live: a person who kills a neighbor unintentionally, without having hated that neighbor before.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And this is the case of the manslayer who may flee there and live: whoever strikes his neighbor without intent and did not hate him previously—

verses.rationale: Keeps the concrete iron/wood accident and fatal outcome; handle is the selected sense of wood, with another reading noted.
verses.before: for example, one goes with his neighbor into the forest to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to cut down the tree, but the iron slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies—he may flee to one of these cities and live.
verses.after: For example, a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood. As he swings his axe to cut a tree, the iron head slips from the handle, strikes his neighbor, and kills him. The man may flee to one of these towns and live.
verses.tsw_comparator: for example, one goes with his neighbor into the forest to cut wood, and his hand swings the axe to cut down the tree, but the iron slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies—he may flee to one of these cities and live.

verses.rationale: Preserves the avenger's hot heart, distance risk, and absence of a death judgment for this killer.
verses.before: Otherwise the avenger of blood may pursue the manslayer while his heart is hot, overtake him because the way is long, and strike his life, though he did not deserve death because he had not hated the man previously.
verses.after: Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue the killer in the heat of anger, overtake him because the journey is long, and kill him. Yet he does not deserve death, because he had not hated his neighbor before.
verses.tsw_comparator: Otherwise the avenger of blood may pursue the manslayer while his heart is hot, overtake him because the way is long, and strike his life, though he did not deserve death because he had not hated the man previously.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated three-town command as the conclusion of the safety rationale.
verses.before: So I command you, saying, ‘Set apart three cities for yourself.’
verses.after: That is why I command you to set apart three towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I command you, saying, ‘Set apart three cities for yourself.’

verses.rationale: Keeps enlargement conditional and grounded in the ancestral oath.
verses.before: “And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory as he swore to your ancestors and gives you all the land that he spoke to give to your ancestors,
verses.after: If the LORD your God enlarges your territory as he swore to your ancestors, giving you all the land he promised them,
verses.tsw_comparator: “And if the LORD your God enlarges your territory as he swore to your ancestors and gives you all the land that he spoke to give to your ancestors,

verses.rationale: Preserves obedience, love, walking, and the explicit three additional towns rather than an unspecified expansion.
verses.before: if you keep all this commandment to do it, which I command you today, to love the LORD your God and walk in his ways all the days, then you will add three more cities for yourself besides these three,
verses.after: as you carefully carry out every command I give you today, loving the LORD your God and walking in his ways always, then add three more towns to these three.
verses.tsw_comparator: if you keep all this commandment to do it, which I command you today, to love the LORD your God and walk in his ways all the days, then you shall add three more cities for yourself besides these three,

verses.rationale: Makes the connection between innocent death and communal bloodguilt readable without deleting either blood term.
verses.before: so that innocent blood is not shed among your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance and bloodguilt comes upon you.
verses.after: This will prevent innocent blood from being shed in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and keep bloodguilt from resting on you.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that innocent blood is not shed in the midst of your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance and bloodguilt comes upon you.

verses.rationale: Retains hatred, ambush, fatal attack, and attempted refuge as the contrasting case.
verses.before: “But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, rises against him, strikes his life so that he dies, and then flees to one of these cities,
verses.after: But suppose a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait, attacks and kills him, and then flees to one of these towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, rises against him, strikes his life so that he dies, and then flees to one of these cities,

verses.rationale: Keeps the killer's local elders responsible for surrender and explicitly states the death outcome.
verses.before: then the elders of his city will send and take him from there and give him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he will die.
verses.after: The elders of his own town must send for him, bring him back, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there and give him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he shall die.

verses.rationale: Preserves the eye image and innocent-blood formula while clarifying guilt as what must be purged.
verses.before: Your eye will not pity him. You will remove the blood of the innocent from Israel, so that it may go well with you.
verses.after: Do not let your eye pity him. Purge the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, so that it may go well with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eye shall not pity him. You shall remove the blood of the innocent from Israel, so that it may go well with you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the earlier boundary setting and inheritance context rather than reducing this to an abstract property rule.
verses.before: “You will not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, which the former generations set in your inheritance that you will inherit in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
verses.after: Do not move your neighbor's boundary marker, set in place by earlier generations, in the inheritance you receive in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, which the former generations set in your inheritance that you will inherit in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.

verses.rationale: Retains the broad offense scope and explicit two-or-three threshold, beyond capital cases alone.
verses.before: “One witness will not rise against a man concerning any guilt or any sin, for any sin that he commits. On the mouth of two witnesses or on the mouth of three witnesses a matter will be established.
verses.after: One witness alone cannot establish a charge against someone for any wrongdoing or sin, whatever the offense. A matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
verses.tsw_comparator: “One witness shall not rise against a man concerning any guilt or any sin, for any sin that he commits. On the mouth of two witnesses or on the mouth of three witnesses a matter shall be established.

verses.rationale: Renders witness of violence as malicious witness, preserving hostile accusation rather than assuming its truth.
verses.before: “If a malicious witness arises against a man to testify against him of rebellion,
verses.after: If a malicious witness comes forward to accuse someone of wrongdoing,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a malicious witness arises against a man to testify against him of rebellion,

verses.rationale: Keeps both disputants, divine presence, and contemporary judicial officials.
verses.before: then the two men who have the dispute will stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in those days.
verses.after: both parties to the dispute must stand before the LORD, before the priests and judges serving at that time.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the two men who have the dispute shall stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in those days.

verses.rationale: Retains careful investigation and the repeated false-witness finding as the penalty's prerequisite.
verses.before: The judges will investigate carefully, and look, if the witness is a false witness and has testified falsely against his brother,
verses.after: The judges must investigate thoroughly. If the witness has lied, giving false testimony against a fellow Israelite,
verses.tsw_comparator: The judges shall investigate carefully, and look, if the witness is a false witness and has testified falsely against his brother,

verses.rationale: Preserves the intended harm as the measure of punishment and the recurring purge formula.
verses.before: then you will do to him as he intended to do to his brother. So you will remove the evil from your midst.
verses.after: do to the witness what he plotted to do to his fellow Israelite. You must purge the evil from among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall do to him as he intended to do to his brother. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deterrent sequence of hearing, fear, and no repetition.
verses.before: The rest will hear and fear and will not again do such an evil thing in your midst.
verses.after: The rest will hear and be afraid, and no one among you will do such an evil thing again.
verses.tsw_comparator: The rest will hear and fear and will not again do such an evil thing in your midst.

verses.rationale: Preserves all five measured correspondences and the eye-of-pity command without substituting a modern penalty scheme.
verses.before: Your eye will not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
verses.after: Do not let your eye pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

verses.rationale: Keeps military asymmetry, both technologies, and the exodus basis of courage.
verses.before: “When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and a people more numerous than you, you will not fear them, for the LORD your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.
verses.after: “When you go to war against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and a force larger than yours, do not be afraid of them. The LORD your God, who brought you up from Egypt, is with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and a people more numerous than you, you shall not fear them, for the LORD your God is with you, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the priest's speech from the officers' later announcements.
verses.before: And when you draw near to battle, the priest will approach and speak to the people.
verses.after: As you approach the battle, the priest is to step forward and address the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you draw near to battle, the priest shall approach and speak to the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves Israel's summons and all four fear prohibitions in an audible speech.
verses.before: He will say to them, ‘Hear, Israel! You are drawing near today to battle against your enemies. Do not let your heart grow weak. Do not fear, panic, or tremble before them.
verses.after: He is to say, ‘Listen, Israel! Today you are approaching battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, panic, or tremble before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall say to them, ‘Hear, Israel! You are drawing near today to battle against your enemies. Do not let your heart grow weak. Do not fear, panic, or tremble before them.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine accompaniment, fighting, and saving as the stated ground; closes the priest's speech.
verses.before: For the LORD your God is the one who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.’
verses.after: The LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and save you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God is the one who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.’

verses.rationale: Retains the house dedication, return, death risk, and another man's enjoyment of the house.
verses.before: “Then the officers will speak to the people, saying, ‘Who is the man who built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it.
verses.after: Then the officers are to tell the people, ‘Has anyone built a new house but not dedicated it? Let him go home, so that he does not die in battle and someone else dedicate it.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then the officers shall speak to the people, saying, ‘Who is the man who built a new house and has not dedicated it? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man dedicate it.

verses.rationale: Renders hillel as beginning ordinary use of the fruit, with the ritual nuance noted rather than adding a harvest date.
verses.before: And who is the man who planted a vineyard and has not begun to enjoy its fruit? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man enjoy it.
verses.after: Has anyone planted a vineyard but not begun to use its fruit? Let him go home, so that he does not die in battle and someone else begin to use it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And who is the man who planted a vineyard and has not begun to enjoy its fruit? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man enjoy it.

verses.rationale: Keeps betrothal distinct from marriage and repeats the full return-and-death pattern.
verses.before: And who is the man who has betrothed a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.’
verses.after: Has anyone become betrothed to a woman but not married her? Let him go home, so that he does not die in battle and another man marry her.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And who is the man who has betrothed a woman and has not taken her? Let him go and return to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the melting-heart image and fear spreading through the force.
verses.before: The officers will speak further to the people and say, ‘Who is the man who is afraid and fainthearted? Let him go and return to his house, so that the heart of his brothers does not melt like his heart.’
verses.after: The officers are also to say, ‘Is anyone afraid and fainthearted? Let him go home, so that he does not make his fellow soldiers' hearts melt like his own.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The officers shall speak further to the people and say, ‘Who is the man who is afraid and fainthearted? Let him go and return to his house, so that the heart of his brothers does not melt like his heart.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the sequence from exemptions to command appointments without identifying an unstated appointing agent.
verses.before: And when the officers have finished speaking to the people, they will appoint commanders of armies at the head of the people.
verses.after: When the officers finish speaking to the people, commanders are to be appointed to lead them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the officers have finished speaking to the people, they shall appoint commanders of armies at the head of the people.

verses.rationale: Renders the call for peace in its siege setting, with the following verse specifying the imposed terms.
verses.before: “When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you will call out peace to it.
verses.after: When you approach a town to fight against it, first offer it terms of peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you draw near to a city to fight against it, you shall call out peace to it.

verses.rationale: Keeps submission and forced labor explicit rather than implying an equal treaty.
verses.before: And if it answers you with peace and opens to you, then all the people found in it will become forced labor for you and will serve you.
verses.after: If it accepts peace and opens its gates to you, all the people found there are to perform forced labor and serve you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if it answers you with peace and opens to you, then all the people found in it shall become forced labor for you and shall serve you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the refusal-and-resistance condition for siege.
verses.before: But if it does not make peace with you but makes war against you, then you will besiege it.
verses.after: If it refuses peace and makes war against you, lay siege to it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if it does not make peace with you but makes war against you, then you shall besiege it.

verses.rationale: Keeps all males and lethal sword language without narrowing the command to combatants.
verses.before: When the LORD your God gives it into your hand, you will strike every male in it with the edge of the sword.
verses.after: When the LORD your God hands it over to you, strike down all its males with the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the LORD your God gives it into your hand, you shall strike every male in it with the edge of the sword.

verses.rationale: Preserves women and children as captives within the plunder list, not merely material goods.
verses.before: But the women, little children, livestock, and everything in the city, all its spoil, you may take as plunder for yourself. You will eat the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God gives you.
verses.after: But take the women, children, livestock, and everything else in the town as plunder for yourselves. You may live on the plunder of the enemies the LORD your God has given you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the women, little children, livestock, and everything in the city, all its spoil, you may take as plunder for yourself. You shall eat the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God gives you.

verses.rationale: Maintains the distinction between distant towns and the nations of the inheritance.
verses.before: Thus you will do to all the cities that are very far from you, which are not from the cities of these nations.
verses.after: This is how you are to treat all the towns far away from you, those that do not belong to these nations here.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus you shall do to all the cities that are very far from you, which are not from the cities of these nations.

verses.rationale: Retains the comprehensive lethal command and its specified territorial scope.
verses.before: “But from the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you will not let anything that breathes live.
verses.after: But in the towns of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, leave alive nothing that breathes.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But from the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall not let anything that breathes live.

verses.rationale: Preserves all six named peoples and the emphatic ban; does not add the seventh name from another list.
verses.before: Rather, you will surely devote them to destruction—the Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite—as the LORD your God commanded you,
verses.after: Devote them completely to destruction—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—as the LORD your God commanded you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rather, you shall surely devote them to destruction—the Hittite, Amorite, Canaanite, Perizzite, Hivite, and Jebusite—as the LORD your God commanded you,

verses.rationale: Keeps the prevention of learned worship practices as the text's stated purpose, without adding justification.
verses.before: so that they do not teach you to do according to all their detestable practices that they have done for their gods and you sin against the LORD your God.
verses.after: Then they will not teach you to do all the detestable things they do for their gods, causing you to sin against the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that they do not teach you to do according to all their detestable practices that they have done for their gods and you sin against the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Selects the rhetorical-question reading of the difficult human/tree clause and retains food trees and prolonged siege.
verses.before: “When you besiege a city many days, fighting against it to capture it, you will not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them, for you may eat from them. You will not cut them down. For is the tree of the field a human being, that it should come before you in the siege?
verses.after: When you besiege a town for a long time, fighting to capture it, do not destroy its trees with the axe. You may eat their fruit; do not cut them down. Is a tree in the field a human being, that it should come under siege from you?
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you besiege a city many days, fighting against it to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them, for you may eat from them. You shall not cut them down. For is the tree of the field a human being, that it should come before you in the siege?

verses.rationale: Preserves the knowledge condition, nonfood distinction, and military use of felled timber.
verses.before: Only a tree that you know is not a tree for food you may destroy and cut down, and you may build siegeworks against the city that makes war with you until it falls.
verses.after: Only trees you know do not produce food may be destroyed and cut down. Use them to build siegeworks against the town making war on you, until it falls.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Only a tree that you know is not a tree for food you may destroy and cut down, and you may build siegeworks against the city that makes war with you until it falls.

verses.rationale: Keeps violent death, discovery in the field, and unknown killer as the ritual's conditions.
verses.before: “If someone is found slain on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, fallen in the field, and it is not known who struck him,
verses.after: “If someone who has been killed is found lying in a field in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess, and no one knows who killed them,
verses.tsw_comparator: “If someone is found slain on the ground that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, fallen in the field, and it is not known who struck him,

verses.rationale: Makes the measurement's starting point and destinations explicit.
verses.before: then your elders and judges will go out and measure the distance from the slain person to the cities around him.
verses.after: your elders and judges must go out and measure the distance from the body to the surrounding towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: then your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distance from the slain person to the cities around him.

verses.rationale: Preserves nearest-town responsibility and both unused-animal conditions.
verses.before: The city nearest to the slain person will be identified, and the elders of that city will take a heifer from the herd that has not been worked and has not pulled in a yoke.
verses.after: The elders of the town nearest the body must take a heifer that has never been worked or pulled a yoke.
verses.tsw_comparator: The city nearest to the slain person shall be identified, and the elders of that city shall take a heifer from the herd that has not been worked and has not pulled in a yoke.

verses.rationale: Selects perennial-flowing sense of nahal ethan, noting rugged-valley alternative; retains uncultivated ground and neck-breaking.
verses.before: The elders of that city will bring the heifer down to a perennial valley that has not been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they will break the heifer’s neck.
verses.after: They must bring the heifer down to a valley with a flowing stream, where the ground has not been worked or sown, and break its neck there in the valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: The elders of that city shall bring the heifer down to a perennial valley that has not been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they shall break the heifer’s neck.

verses.rationale: Keeps Levitical identity and both judicial categories; injury is qualified for possible ritual affliction in notes.
verses.before: Then the priests, the sons of Levi, will approach, for the LORD your God has chosen them to minister to him and to bless in the name of the LORD, and by their mouth every dispute and every assault will be decided.
verses.after: The priests, the sons of Levi, are to come forward. The LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and bless in the LORD's name, and every dispute and case of injury is to be decided by their word.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the priests, the sons of Levi, shall approach, for the LORD your God has chosen them to minister to him and to bless in the name of the LORD, and by their mouth every dispute and every assault shall be decided.

verses.rationale: Retains all elders, the repeated nearest-town designation, and the concrete handwashing location.
verses.before: All the elders of that city nearest to the slain person will wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
verses.after: All the elders of the town nearest the body must wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the elders of that city nearest to the slain person shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley.

verses.rationale: Keeps both bodily images and translates the written/read shed verb once, following the plural reading.
verses.before: They will answer and say, ‘Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
verses.after: They must declare, ‘Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it happen.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall answer and say, ‘Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.

verses.rationale: Keeps atonement, redemption, repeated Israel, and the shift from prayer to assurance.
verses.before: Make atonement for your people Israel, whom you redeemed, O LORD, and do not place innocent blood among your people Israel.’ Then the bloodguilt will be atoned for them.
verses.after: Make atonement for your people Israel, whom you redeemed, LORD. Do not lay the guilt of innocent blood on your people Israel.’ Then atonement will be made for their bloodguilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Make atonement for your people Israel, whom you redeemed, O LORD, and do not place innocent blood in the midst of your people Israel.’ Then the bloodguilt shall be atoned for them.

verses.rationale: Retains the innocent-blood formula and divine-eye standard as the ritual's conclusion.
verses.before: So you will remove innocent blood from your midst when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.after: In this way you will purge the guilt of innocent blood from among you by doing what is right in the LORD's eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you shall remove innocent blood from your midst when you do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps war and captivity explicit before the following marriage case.
verses.before: “When you go out to war against your enemies and the LORD your God gives them into your hand and you take them captive,
verses.after: When you go to war against your enemies, the LORD your God hands them over to you, and you take captives,
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you go out to war against your enemies and the LORD your God gives them into your hand and you take them captive,

verses.rationale: Retains beauty because the source specifies it, the captor's desire, and the captive's status without inventing consent.
verses.before: and you see among the captives a woman beautiful in form, and you desire her and would take her for yourself as wife,
verses.after: if you see a beautiful woman among the captives, desire her, and would take her as your wife,
verses.tsw_comparator: and you see among the captives a woman beautiful in form, and you desire her and would take her for yourself as wife,

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily preparation; trim selects a sense of do the nails, with the alternative noted.
verses.before: then you will bring her into your house. She will shave her head and trim her nails.
verses.after: bring her into your house. She is to shave her head and trim her nails.
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall bring her into your house. She shall shave her head and trim her nails.

verses.rationale: Keeps removal of captive clothing, both parents, a full month of mourning, and explicit sexual and marital action.
verses.before: She will remove the garment of her captivity from upon her and remain in your house and weep for her father and mother a full month. After that you may go in to her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.

verses.after: The LORD your God walks through your camp to rescue you and hand your enemies over to you. Your camp must be holy. He must not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD your God walks in the midst of your camp to deliver you and to give your enemies before you. Therefore your camp shall be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unqualified wording of the non-return command without inserting an unstated nationality limitation.
verses.before: “You will not hand over to his master a servant who has escaped from his master to you.
verses.after: Do not hand a slave back to the master from whom he has escaped to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not hand over to his master a servant who has escaped from his master to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps the escaped slave's choice of residence and the explicit non-oppression command.
verses.before: He will live with you, in your midst, in the place he chooses within one of your gates, wherever is good for him. You will not oppress him.
verses.after: Let him live among you, in whatever town he chooses, wherever suits him. Do not mistreat him.

verses.rationale: Preserves female and male qedeshah/qadesh with the traditional rendering; notes the uncertainty of the roles rather than inventing ritual details.

verses.tsw_comparator: “There shall be no cult prostitute among the daughters of Israel, and there shall be no cult prostitute among the sons of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains the literal dog term and separate payment nouns, with the possible male-prostitute interpretation in the apparatus.

verses.after: Do not bring a prostitute's earnings or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God to fulfill any vow. Both are detestable to the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not bring the wages of a prostitute or the price of a dog into the house of the LORD your God for any vow, for both of these are detestable to the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three loan categories and does not narrow the ban to excessive rates.

verses.after: Do not charge your fellow Israelite interest on silver, food, or anything else lent at interest.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not charge interest to your brother—interest on silver, interest on food, interest on anything that is lent at interest.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit distinction between foreigner and fellow Israelite and the land blessing.
verses.before: You may charge interest to a foreigner, but to your brother you will not charge interest, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess.
verses.after: You may charge a foreigner interest, but not your fellow Israelite, so that the LORD your God may bless everything you undertake in the land you are entering to possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: You may charge interest to a foreigner, but to your brother you shall not charge interest, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all to which you put your hand in the land that you are entering to possess.

verses.rationale: Preserves voluntary vow becoming binding and the emphatic divine requirement.

verses.after: If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not delay in fulfilling it. The LORD your God will surely require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you vow a vow to the LORD your God, you shall not delay to pay it, for the LORD your God will surely require it from you, and it will be sin in you.

verses.rationale: Keeps freedom not to vow as a separate counterbalancing instruction.
verses.before: But if you refrain from vowing, it will not be sin in you.
verses.after: But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you refrain from vowing, it will not be sin in you.

verses.rationale: Retains lips and mouth imagery with voluntary speech and obligatory performance.
verses.before: What goes out from your lips you will keep and do, just as you voluntarily vowed to the LORD your God, what you spoke with your mouth.
verses.after: Be careful to do what has passed your lips, whatever you freely vowed to the LORD your God and spoke with your mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: What goes out from your lips you shall keep and do, just as you voluntarily vowed to the LORD your God, what you spoke with your mouth.

verses.rationale: Keeps permission for immediate eating and the prohibition on collecting to carry away.

verses.after: When you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat grapes until you are satisfied, but put none in your basket.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat grapes according to your desire, until you are satisfied, but you shall not put any into your vessel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the hand-versus-sickle distinction and repeated neighbor ownership.

verses.after: When you enter your neighbor's standing grain, you may pluck heads by hand, but do not swing a sickle through your neighbor's grain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When you enter your neighbor’s standing grain, you may pluck ears with your hand, but you shall not swing a sickle against your neighbor’s standing grain.

verses.rationale: Keeps the one-year exemption, military and other duty scope, and the wife's joy as its purpose.

verses.rationale: Preserves both mill and upper-stone restriction and the life image rather than merely calling the object valuable.

verses.after: Do not take a pair of millstones, or even the upper stone, as a pledge. That would be taking someone's life as a pledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: “No one shall take a handmill or an upper millstone as a pledge, for that would be taking a life as a pledge.

verses.rationale: Keeps kidnapping, enslavement, sale, Israelite scope, and death as the stated sanction.

verses.after: If a man is caught kidnapping one of his fellow Israelites, treating that person as a slave and selling them, that kidnapper must die. You must purge the evil from among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If a man is found kidnapping one of his brothers from the children of Israel, treating him as merchandise or selling him, then that kidnapper shall die. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.

verses.rationale: Renders tsaraat without equating it with modern leprosy and retains priestly instructions and Moses' command.

verses.after: In a case of a defiling skin disease, take great care to do everything the Levitical priests instruct you. Carefully follow what I commanded them.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Be careful concerning an outbreak of skin disease, to guard diligently and do according to all that the Levitical priests instruct you. As I commanded them, so you shall be careful to do.

verses.rationale: Keeps Miriam by name and the journey setting rather than replacing the reminder with a retelling.
verses.before: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out from Egypt.
verses.after: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the road after you came out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves the borrower's household boundary and the broad loan scope.
verses.before: “When you lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you will not enter his house to take his pledge.
verses.after: When you make any loan to your neighbor, do not enter the house to take the pledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not enter his house to take his pledge.

verses.rationale: Makes the creditor wait and the borrower act, preserving the allocation of agency.
verses.before: You will stand outside, and the man to whom you lend will bring the pledge outside to you.
verses.after: Stand outside. The person receiving your loan must bring the pledge out to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall stand outside, and the man to whom you lend shall bring the pledge outside to you.

verses.rationale: Retains the overnight restriction specifically for a poor borrower.
verses.before: And if he is a poor man, you will not sleep with his pledge.
verses.after: If that person is poor, do not go to sleep keeping the pledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge.

verses.rationale: Keeps sunset, the cloak's function, the borrower's blessing, and righteousness as the divine assessment.
verses.before: You will surely return the pledge to him when the sun goes down, so that he may sleep in his garment and bless you. It will be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
verses.after: Be sure to return it at sunset, so that your neighbor can sleep in the cloak and bless you. This will count as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall surely return the pledge to him when the sun goes down, so that he may sleep in his garment and bless you. It will be righteousness for you before the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Preserves both protected worker categories and the paired poor-and-needy description.
verses.before: “You will not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether one of your brothers or one of the resident aliens who is in your land within your gates.
verses.after: Do not exploit a poor and needy hired worker, whether a fellow Israelite or a resident foreigner living in your land, in your towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not oppress a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether one of your brothers or one of the resident aliens who is in your land within your gates.

verses.rationale: Keeps same-day payment, dependence, appeal to God, and the employer's liability.
verses.before: On his day you will give him his wages before the sun goes down, for he is poor and sets his life upon it, lest he cry against you to the LORD and it become sin in you.
verses.after: Pay the wages that same day, before sunset. The worker is poor and depends on them. Otherwise the worker may cry to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: On his day you shall give him his wages before the sun goes down, for he is poor and sets his life upon it, lest he cry against you to the LORD and it become sin in you.

verses.rationale: Renders collective fathers as parents in this general legal rule, retaining both directions and individual liability.
verses.before: “Fathers will not be put to death for sons, and sons will not be put to death for fathers. Each person will be put to death for his own sin.
verses.after: Parents must not be put to death for their children, nor children for their parents. Each must be put to death only for their own sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, and sons shall not be put to death for fathers. Each person shall be put to death for his own sin.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two justice recipients distinct from the widow's separate pledge protection.
verses.before: “You will not distort the justice of the resident alien or the orphan, and you will not take a widow’s garment as a pledge.
verses.after: Do not deny justice to the resident foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow's garment as a pledge.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not distort the justice of the resident alien or the orphan, and you shall not take a widow’s garment as a pledge.

verses.rationale: Preserves slavery and redemption as the explicit ground of these protections.
verses.before: You will remember that you were a servant in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. Therefore I command you to do this thing.
verses.after: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall remember that you were a servant in Egypt and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. Therefore I command you to do this thing.

verses.rationale: Keeps accidental forgotten sheaf, no return, all three recipients, and hand-work blessing.
verses.before: “When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you will not return to take it. It will be for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
verses.after: When you harvest your field and forget a sheaf, do not go back for it. Leave it for the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless all the work of your hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you reap your harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, you shall not return to take it. It shall be for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.

verses.rationale: Preserves olive beating and the ban on a second pass, repeating the full recipient list.
verses.before: When you beat your olive tree, you will not go over the branches again. What remains will be for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow.
verses.after: When you beat your olive trees, do not go over the branches again. Leave what remains for the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the branches again. What remains shall be for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow.

verses.rationale: Keeps the separate vineyard rule and the third repetition of protected recipients.
verses.before: When you harvest your vineyard, you will not glean it again afterward. What remains will be for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow.
verses.after: When you gather your grapes, do not glean the vineyard afterward. Leave what remains for the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean it again afterward. What remains shall be for the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated slavery-memory conclusion rather than deleting it as redundant with verse 18.

verses.after: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt. Therefore I command you to do this thing.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the judicial actors and preserves both opposed verdicts.
verses.before: “If there is a dispute between men and they come to judgment, and the judges judge them, acquitting the righteous and condemning the wicked,
verses.after: “When people have a dispute and bring it to court, the judges must decide between them, acquitting the innocent and condemning the guilty.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If there is a dispute between men and they come to judgment, and the judges judge them, acquitting the righteous and condemning the wicked,

verses.rationale: Keeps corporal punishment, posture, supervision, and proportional counting without softening the physical act.
verses.before: then if the wicked person deserves beating, the judge will make him lie down and be beaten before him according to the measure of his wickedness, by number.
verses.after: If the guilty person deserves a beating, the judge must have him lie down and be beaten in the judge's presence, with the number of blows suited to the offense.
verses.tsw_comparator: then if the wicked person deserves beating, the judge shall make him lie down and be beaten before him according to the measure of his wickedness, by number.

verses.rationale: Retains forty rather than the later thirty-nine practice, and degradation of one's fellow as the limit's stated reason.
verses.before: Forty blows he may give him, but no more, lest he continue to beat him beyond these with many blows and your brother be degraded in your eyes.
verses.after: Forty blows may be given, but no more. If more are added, your fellow Israelite may be degraded in your eyes by the excessive beating.
verses.tsw_comparator: Forty blows he may give him, but no more, lest he continue to beat him beyond these with many blows and your brother be degraded in your eyes.

verses.rationale: Retains the compact concrete prohibition rather than substituting its later applications.
verses.before: “You will not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.
verses.after: Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.
verses.tsw_comparator: “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

verses.rationale: Keeps co-resident brothers, no son, outside-marriage ban, and the brother-in-law's sexual/marital duty; child alternative is noted.

verses.after: If brothers live together and one dies without a son, his widow must not marry a man outside the family. Her husband's brother must have sex with her, take her as his wife, and fulfill a brother-in-law's duty to her.
verses.tsw_comparator: “If brothers live together and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead man shall not marry outside the family to a foreign man. Her husband’s brother shall go in to her, take her to himself as wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother for her.

verses.rationale: Preserves firstborn and continuing the deceased's name without requiring the same personal given name.

verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not have in your house differing measures, a large and a small.

verses.rationale: Repeats full and honest for both standards and preserves the land-and-life promise.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated everyone and broadens from the specific fraud to injustice as the source does.

verses.before: you will take from the first of all the fruit of the ground that you bring in from your land that the LORD your God is giving you, put it in a basket, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose to make his name dwell there.
verses.after: take some of the first of every crop you harvest from the ground of the land the LORD your God gives you. Put it in a basket and go to the place the LORD your God chooses for his name to dwell.
verses.tsw_comparator: you shall take from the first of all the fruit of the ground that you bring in from your land that the LORD your God is giving you, put it in a basket, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose to make his name dwell there.

verses.rationale: Retains your God addressed to the priest, rather than adopting the my God variant; keeps singular declarant within communal promise.
verses.before: You will come to the priest who is in those days and say to him, ‘I declare today to the LORD your God that I have entered the land that the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us.’
verses.after: Go to the priest serving at that time and say, ‘Today I declare to the LORD your God that I have entered the land the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us.’
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall come to the priest who is in those days and say to him, ‘I declare today to the LORD your God that I have entered the land that the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us.’

verses.rationale: Keeps the handover and placement at the altar as distinct actions.
verses.before: Then the priest will take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the LORD your God.
verses.after: The priest must take the basket from your hand and set it before the altar of the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Selects wandering for oved while noting perishing; preserves father, Aramean, resident status, and few-to-many movement.
verses.before: And you will answer and say before the LORD your God: ‘A wandering Aramean was my father. He went down to Egypt and sojourned there, few in number, and there he became a great, mighty, and numerous nation.
verses.after: Then declare before the LORD your God, ‘My father was a wandering Aramean. He went down to Egypt and lived there as a foreigner with only a few people. There he became a great nation, mighty and numerous.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall answer and say before the LORD your God: ‘A wandering Aramean was my father. He went down to Egypt and sojourned there, few in number, and there he became a great, mighty, and numerous nation.

verses.rationale: Keeps the shift from ancestor to first-person plural confession and all three forms of harm.
verses.before: The Egyptians treated us badly, afflicted us, and laid hard service upon us.
verses.after: The Egyptians treated us harshly, afflicted us, and imposed hard labor on us.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Egyptians treated us badly, afflicted us, and laid hard service upon us.

verses.rationale: Preserves hearing and seeing, repeated LORD, and the three suffering nouns.
verses.before: Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our labor, and our oppression.
verses.after: We cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors. The LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our toil, and our oppression.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our affliction, our labor, and our oppression.

verses.rationale: Keeps both bodily images and all three accompanying manifestations rather than replacing them with power alone.
verses.before: The LORD brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, and with signs and wonders.
verses.after: The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, signs, and wonders.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD brought us out from Egypt with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, and with signs and wonders.

verses.rationale: Retains the deictic this place/this land and the recurring abundance image.
verses.before: He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.after: He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.

verses.rationale: Marks the shift back to singular offering and then out of the worshiper's speech into instruction.
verses.before: And now, look, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that you, O LORD, have given me.’ Then you will set it before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.
verses.after: Now, LORD, I bring the first of the fruit of the ground you have given me.’ Set it before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, look, I have brought the first of the fruit of the ground that you, O LORD, have given me.’ Then you shall set it before the LORD your God and bow down before the LORD your God.

verses.rationale: Keeps household blessing and both explicitly included groups in the rejoicing.
verses.before: You will rejoice in all the good that the LORD your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the resident alien who is in your midst.
verses.after: Rejoice in all the good the LORD your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the resident foreigner among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall rejoice in all the good that the LORD your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the resident alien who is in your midst.

verses.rationale: Retains third year, whole tithe, four recipients, local provision, and satisfaction.
verses.before: “When you finish tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, resident alien, orphan, and widow, so that they may eat within your gates and be satisfied,
verses.after: When you finish setting aside the whole tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, give it to the Levite, the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, so that they may eat their fill in your towns.
verses.tsw_comparator: “When you finish tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, resident alien, orphan, and widow, so that they may eat within your gates and be satisfied,

verses.rationale: Keeps first-person accounting, repeated recipients, and both non-transgression and non-forgetting claims.
verses.before: then you will say before the LORD your God: ‘I have removed the holy portion from my house and also given it to the Levite, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, according to all your commandment that you commanded me. I have not transgressed your commandments, and I have not forgotten.
verses.after: Then say before the LORD your God, ‘I have removed the sacred portion from my house and given it to the Levite, the resident foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not transgressed your commands or forgotten them.
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall say before the LORD your God: ‘I have removed the holy portion from my house and also given it to the Levite, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, according to all your commandment that you commanded me. I have not transgressed your commandments, and I have not forgotten.

verses.rationale: Preserves three distinct denials, including the obscure dead-related use, without inventing a particular ritual.
verses.before: I have not eaten from it in my mourning, nor removed any of it while unclean, nor given any of it for the dead. I have listened to the voice of the LORD my God; I have done according to all that you commanded me.
verses.after: I have eaten none of it while mourning, removed none while unclean, and given none to the dead. I have listened to the LORD my God and done everything you commanded me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have not eaten from it in my mourning, nor removed any of it while unclean, nor given any of it for the dead. I have listened to the voice of the LORD my God; I have done according to all that you commanded me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the heavenly dwelling, people and land blessing, oath, and repeated milk-and-honey image.
verses.before: Look down from your holy dwelling, from the heavens, and bless your people Israel and the ground that you have given us, as you swore to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.’
verses.after: Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the ground you have given us, as you swore to our ancestors—a land flowing with milk and honey.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Look down from your holy dwelling, from the heavens, and bless your people Israel and the ground that you have given us, as you swore to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.’

verses.rationale: Retains today, both instruction categories, and full heart-and-soul obedience.
verses.before: “This day the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and judgments. You will keep and do them with all your heart and with all your life.
verses.after: Today the LORD your God commands you to carry out these statutes and judgments. Take care to practice them with all your heart and all your soul.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This day the LORD your God commands you to do these statutes and judgments. You shall keep and do them with all your heart and with all your life.

verses.rationale: Renders the rare causative declaration verb within the mutual covenant affirmation; keeps every human obligation.
verses.before: You have declared today that the LORD is your God, that you will walk in his ways, keep his statutes, commandments, and judgments, and listen to his voice.
verses.after: Today you have declared the LORD to be your God, promising to walk in his ways, keep his statutes, commands, and judgments, and listen to his voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: You have declared today that the LORD is your God, that you will walk in his ways, keep his statutes, commandments, and judgments, and listen to his voice.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reciprocal declaration and the obligation attached to treasured status, without making God the keeper of the commands.
verses.before: And the LORD has declared today that you are his treasured people, as he spoke to you, and that you are to keep all his commandments,
verses.after: And today the LORD has declared that you are to be his treasured people, as he promised you, and that you are to keep all his commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD has declared today that you are his treasured people, as he spoke to you, and that you are to keep all his commandments,

verses.rationale: Keeps comparative elevation, all three honor terms, and holiness as the concluding purpose.
verses.before: and that he will set you high above all the nations that he has made, for praise, fame, and honor, and that you will be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he spoke.”
verses.after: He will set you high above all the nations he has made, in praise, renown, and honor, so that you may be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he promised.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and that he will set you high above all the nations that he has made, for praise, fame, and honor, and that you will be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he spoke.”
